_readme: THE PLATFORM'S FORECAST TREND THRESHOLDS — the bands the Three-Way Forecast's
two-year trend read draws (item 4.61 phase (b)).
🔴 EVERY NUMBER IN HERE IS MIKE'S, AND AN EMPTY ONE STAYS EMPTY. He ruled on
2026-09-03 that the bands fire on thresholds HE sets, against a recommendation of a
plain read with no judgement — and the reason that ruling is safe is precisely that
the numbers are his. A plausible-looking default invented by a developer would put
advisory judgement into a funding document with nobody's name on it, which is the
one thing this file must never do. DO NOT FILL A NULL IN. An absent threshold is a
supported setting: the measure is shown in full with both years and its movement,
and simply is not banded.
TWO BASES, AND THE SPLIT IS RULED (2026-09-03, rulings 6 and 7).
levels    — the three day-counts band on THIS YEAR'S LEVEL. A level is what an
accountant reads on a day-count and it travels across trades.
Each carries its OWN numbers: 46 days means a quite different thing
about a customer, a supplier and a shelf. Sharing one set turned a
worked example red on all three, two of them for figures nobody would
blink at.
movements — the three percentage measures band on the MOVEMENT between the two
years. A level would not travel: a gross margin that is alarming for a
retailer is routine for a builder, whereas a margin that fell three
points is worth a look in any trade.
EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS MIKE'S, GIVEN 2026-09-03, ONE PAIR AT A TIME. `green` and
`amber` are the TOP of each band, so red is anything above `amber`.
debtorDays    35 / 45 — his own words, "0-35 = green - 36 - 45 - orange - 46 + =
red". The classic figures: 30-day terms, 45 slipping, 46+ late.
creditorDays  35 / 45 — "same as debtor is fine".
stockDays     30 / 60 — "0-30 is green - 31-60 is orange - 61+ is red". Deliberately
wider than the other two: stock days measure how long goods sit on a
shelf, and a business holding three months is at 90 and may be trading
perfectly normally.
salesGrowth   amber below 0%, red below -5% — accepted as a starting point. It reads
DOWNWARDS, so the red figure is the LOWER one.
grossMargin   amber 1 pt, red 3 pts of fall — accepted.
overheadRatio amber 1 pt, red 3 pts of rise — accepted. The same pair as gross
margin, and not merely for symmetry: a point of margin lost and a point
of overheads gained cost exactly the same money, because both are a
point of sales.
HE CALLED THESE "a place to start" AND ASKED TWICE THAT THEY BE EDITABLE. They are —
the mentor's Forecast Trend Thresholds tab under Model Inputs, with version history and
restore. Changing one there does NOT change this file; it stores the mentor's own
overlay over it, which is how every other cascading setting in this app works.
THIS FILE IS THE MENTOR TIER'S. A firm gets its own copy only if one ever has a real
reason to differ — the default-is-mentor-alone ruling of 2026-08-24. The resolver
(server/utils/forecastTrendThresholds.js) already walks the tier chain, so that day
costs one line in TAB_TIERS and nothing here.
